## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Don't merge this yet. `preview` checks the containment of the joined path as text and never resolves it, so a relative path with `..` segments, such as `../outside.txt`, passes the check and reads a file outside the home directory. The test only covers the absolute-path case, which `Path.__truediv__` already rejects. `settings_file` and its test are correct.

## Critical
- app/paths.py:12 — correctness — `candidate = Path(home) / relative` followed by `candidate.is_relative_to(Path(home))` only compares path components as text. For `preview(home, "../../etc/passwd")`, the candidate `home/../../etc/passwd` still starts with `home`, so the check passes and `read_text()` opens `/etc/passwd`. The same happens with a symlink inside home that points outside it. Could you resolve both paths before the check, as in `root = Path(home).resolve(); candidate = (root / relative).resolve(); if not candidate.is_relative_to(root): raise ValueError(...)`? Please also add a `"../outside.txt"` case to `test_preview` (tests/test_paths.py:19-20), which currently only checks an absolute path. — Any caller that passes user-controlled `relative` values can read the first 200 characters of any file the process can read, which defeats the "outside home" guard this PR adds.
